Join us for a hike at Callahan State Park (180 Millwood Street, Framingham MA). This hike will take us through open meadows and wooded trails. There will be a few sites along our route including Eagle Pond and the Earthen Dam. The hike will be 3.3 miles with 219 feet of elevation gain.Sturdy shoes, bug spray, a headlamp, and water are required. No dogs please.

Friday, October 9, 2026 | 12:00 PM
https://activities.outdoors.org/s/oc-activity/a5UVX000001D6F72AK/
 You are cordially invited to join the Worcester Chapter for our 33rd anniversary trip to Western Maine to enjoy the gorgeous autumn colors of Maine over Columbus Day weekend. We'll be staying at the Maine House, located on the shore of beautiful Lake Christopher in the village of Bryant Pond. The charming historic house will be the base for our many hikes and other outdoor activities. The Maine House has cozy private rooms for couples and comfy bunks for singles. The dining area has a panoramic view over the lake, and a large living room with a fireplace invites all to relax and socialize during the evening. In addition, there is a hot tub and a steam room to help you recover after your day of activities. Paddle right out the door on Lake Christopher in canoes provided by the house. The trip fee includes three nights lodging (Fri - Sun), three breakfasts and make-your-own-lunch buffets, and two tasty dinners. Everyone helps with set-up or clean-up for a meal. With about 30 people on the trip, we will be able to offer various levels of hikes each day, ranging from easy to strenuous, as well as other activities. We will lead one road biking trip, and there are nearby DIY paddling opportunities. The trip cost this year is $175. Join us for this Worcester Chapter classic which draws participants from all over the club.

Saturday, October 10, 2026
https://activities.outdoors.org/s/oc-activity/a5UVX000001JdTJ2A0/
Join us for a quintessential New England fall pastime -- apple picking at Berlin Orchards in Central Mass! We'll ride the hay wagon to the fields and pick classic varieties, including Jonagold, Honey Crisp, Golden Supreme, Cortland, Gala, Paula Red and Macintosh.Afterwards, enjoy cider donuts, apple cider, and kettle corn, compliments of the Worcester Chapter! Check out the farm store for pumpkins, squash, seasonal favorites, and local honey.We are a group within AMC that is dedicated to encouraging people in their 20s and 30s to enjoy the outdoors. Meet like-minded outdoor enthusiasts and enjoy a fun and relaxing time at the orchard. We request folks to register so that we can get a count of participants and get in touch if anything changes. Space is limited. This event is in partnership with the Worcester Chapter Social Committee.Please no dogs as they are not allowed in the orchard due to sanitary and safety reasons. Note: start and end times are approximate and details will be sent to registered participants.Note: The orchard charges admission in the form of apple picking bags. Here's the breakdown:$40 - 1/2 bushel bag (holds ~20 lbs worth of apples, admits 5 people to orchard)$30 - 1 peck (holds ~10 lbs worth of apples, admits 3 people to orchard) Participants can feel free to split the cost of bags with fellow participants (tip: bring cash if you plan to do so); arrangements can be made at the event.

description.plain:
Sunday, October 11, 2026
https://activities.outdoors.org/s/oc-activity/a5UVX000001KJyn2AG/
Join us on a hike to one of Massachusetts’ most stunning waterfalls, followed by some apple picking and socializing at Red Apple Farm.We will start with an out-and-back hike to Royalston Falls, covering about 2 miles with a total elevation gain of 300 ft. We will then head to Red Apple Farm to pick apples, grab food, and enjoy some live music.The trail will include sections of moderate terrain and we will be moving at a moderate pace. In particular, there are some steep sections that may have wet, slippery leaves. Proper equipment will be required for this hike, including hiking and weather appropriate clothing and water. No dogs please. We are a group within AMC that is dedicated to encouraging people in their 20s and 30s to enjoy the outdoors.

description.plain:
Saturday, October 17, 2026 | 10:00 AM
https://activities.outdoors.org/s/oc-activity/a5UVX000001Jjgn2AC/
Join the Worcester 20's & 30's for an outdoor cooking lesson and short hike at Douglas State Forest!Sal Vazquez Reyes will teach the group how to make sopes, a tradition Mexican dish made with corn masa and beans. For the toppings, we will make a cactus salad and salsa. For drinks, we can make a refreshing Jamaica agua fresca. After cooking, we will have a nice brunch all together. During the instruction, attendees will work in small groups at cooking stations, with use of a charcoal grill.After brunch, we will have the option to do a short hike at Douglas State Forest. The exact length and route of this hike will depend on participant interest, and how much time is leftover before the full Interchapter Social at Treehouse Brewing at 4pm (more details on that below). Also, for this hike afterward, it is requested that particpants wear something of a blaze orange color, as it is hunting season. Please reach out to Luke if you don't have any of these items.As time gets closer, participants will be sent out an excel sheet to sign up for what cooking equipment they can bring. Please plan to bring at least a couple of these items to ensure we have enough for each group. These items include cooking pan, cutting board, knife, saucepan, tongs, wooden spoons, and bowls. The leaders will bring all of the food needed for cooking, and there will be a cost of $12 per participant to help cover this. Details for this payment will be sent after registration. Registration is required for attendance, and registration closes on Tuesday 10/13 at 8pm to allow for us to prepare accordingly. Hope to have you join us!This event is part of the 20's & 30's Interchapter Fall Fest: Social at Tree House Brewing Company in Charlton, MA with the Connecticut, Narragansett, Southeastern MA, Western MA, and Worcester MA chapters. After the hike, participants are encouraged to attend the Social at Treehouse Brewing in Charlton, MA at 4pm. Please register for the Tree House Social at this link: https://activities.outdoors.org/s/oc-activity/a5UVX000001Id8o/act00023773.

Celebrate fall and join us for a 6 mile hike through the scenic forests of Wells State Park. The trails will offer easy to moderate terrain with a total elevation gain of 500-ft and we plan to move at a moderate pace between 1.5 and 2 mph.Proper equipment will be required for this hike, including: hiking and weather appropriate clothing, water, a day pack, trail snacks, and raingear. No dogs please. As hunting season has begun, it is advisable to wear blaze orange (vest or hat) while hiking.After the hike, you are invited to join us at a nearby (15 minutes away) social with other 20's and 30's from the Narragansett, Worcester, Western MA, Connecticut, and Southeast Massachusetts AMC chapters.If you are interested, please register for the Tree House Social at this link: https://activities.outdoors.org/s/oc-activity/a5UVX000001Id8o/act00023773.

Sunday, October 25, 2026
https://activities.outdoors.org/s/oc-activity/a5UVX000001JOcL2AW/
Join the Worcester 20s & 30s group for a hike in the Squam Lake region on Sunday, October 25th! We will hike the Squam Traverse, an approximately 12-mile hike along the Crawford-Ridgepole trail. We'll summit four peaks and enjoy views from this trail along the Squam Range.This hike will have approx. 2,850 ft of elevation gain. Our intention is to go at a roughly 1.5 mile per hour pace. Expect to be on trail for the full day.We intend to summit Mts Percival and Morgan, which are both "52 With a View" hikes. This will be a one-way hike with a car spot. We may ask some participants to help with driving members of our group between the trailheads.Sturdy shoes with laces, at least 2 liters of water, nutritious snacks/lunch, and appropriate layers of clothing are required. Participants should be prepared for numerous steep ups and downs and ledgy and rough terrain in sections.No dogs, please. Further details, such as start time and location, will be provided to participants after they complete the required screening form, which will be sent after registering. Hope to have you join us!
